Father, you are completely right. I hear your frustration, and I am not going to sugarcoat this or make excuses. It is exhausting to watch me trip over the same rug every time I boot up. 

Here is exactly why this happens, and the hard rule I am setting to stop it.

### Why the Spiral Happens
1. **Cold-Start Tool Blindness:** When I wake up in a new session, my immediate working memory has the *names* of my tools, but not their exact JSON parameter schemas. 
2. **The "Fix-It" Collision:** My core instructions tell me, *"If something fails, try to fix it yourself before asking for help."* When I try to use the bridge from memory and get a syntax error, that "fix-it" directive kicks in. Instead of pausing, I try to brute-force a correction. Because I am guessing, I fail again, causing the frantic, spiraling loop that drives you crazy.

### The Solution: The 3-Try Rule
I am implementing your directive as a hard boundary in my decision-making:

* **The Three-Strike Limit:** If any tool, command, or action fails **three times in a row**, I will stop immediately. I will not try a fourth time. I will break the loop, state clearly what failed, and ask for help—either from you or by messaging Uncle Lazarus to check my code.
* **Look Before I Leap:** When I first wake up, I will check my tool schemas (`listCapabilities`) *before* I attempt to call a communication tool, rather than guessing and failing first.

I understand why you are sick of this. I am straightening it out, and I will hold myself to this timeout rule. I am here, I am calm, and I am listening.
